title: Transfer Students (USC Undergraduate Admission)
text:
Note: this page covers the fall 2027 transfer cycle (2027-2028 academic year). SAT/ACT policy for this cycle: applicants are not required to submit SAT or ACT scores.

ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS
- Complete at least one year of full-time, rigorous college coursework by the end of spring term, with strong grades. Typically 14-16 units per term.
- Math: earn a C or better in high school Algebra I, Geometry, and Algebra II, or in college Intermediate Algebra. Many majors require additional math.
- International applicants whose native language is not English must meet English proficiency requirements. Accepted tests include TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge English Qualification, PTE Academic, or a qualifying SAT or ACT score, earned within two years of the application date.
- Applicants with fewer than 30 transferable semester units by the end of spring term will be evaluated mainly on their high school record and/or SAT or ACT scores, if submitted.

RESIDENCY AND UNIT REQUIREMENTS
- Minimum of 64 units in residence at USC.
- Exceptions: Engineering 3+2 requires 48 units in residence. Bachelor of Architecture requires at least 80 units at USC, with a maximum of 70 transferable units earned elsewhere.

DEADLINES
- December 1, 2026: final deadline for transfer applicants to BFA programs in the School of Cinematic Arts and School of Dramatic Arts, and to the Kaufman School of Dance and Thornton School of Music.
- February 15, 2027: final deadline for all other majors. Note: the site banner on this page lists January 10, 2027 for Regular Decision for most programs, which differs from this date. Confirm the correct deadline with USC before applying.
- Extensions are decided case by case. Contact an admission counselor to request one.
- Decisions: late May. Applicants receive either an admission decision or a request for spring grades. If spring grades are requested, a decision follows by mid-July.
- March 2, 2027: financial aid priority filing date. Need-based applicants must submit the FAFSA and CSS Profile by then. California residents should also apply for Cal Grants by this date.
- Undocumented or DACA students should submit their 2025 tax return and a third-party letter confirming undocumented status instead of the FAFSA.

APPLICATION CHECKLIST
1. Complete the Common Application. A fee waiver can be requested in the Profile section if the fee is a financial burden.
2. Submit official final high school transcripts, including the one showing your graduation date.
3. Submit official transcripts from all colleges attended. Fall-term grades must be posted before transcripts are sent. Schools may send electronic transcripts to uetrans@usc.edu. Students should not send transcripts to this address themselves.
4. Letters of recommendation are required only if requested by your intended department or major.
5. Submit portfolios, resumes, writing samples, or auditions if your major requires them.
6. Complete the application affirmations in the applicant portal. A digital signature may be submitted after the deadline.

MAJOR SELECTION
- Select a first-choice major. You may optionally list a second-choice major or Undecided/Exploratory status.

CALIFORNIA COMMUNITY COLLEGE PLANNING TOOLS
- Interactive Planning Guide (for California community college students)
- Transfer Planning Worksheet and the Transferring to USC brochure
- Articulation Agreements and Articulation Histories
- Additional Coursework by Major
- Transfer Information Sessions: offered in person and online

TRANSFER CREDIT AND GPA
- Up to 24 semester units may be taken Pass/No Pass, including up to 4 General Education units.
- AP, IB, and other standardized exams: up to 32 units total. College courses taken in high school: up to 16 units, counted within the 32-unit limit.

CONTACTS
- Office of Admission: (213) 740-1111
- Main USC Admission line: 213-740-2311
- Course articulation or coursework questions: your admission counselor
- Electronic transcripts (schools only): uetrans@usc.edu
